analysis: The trial completed successfully but achieved macro validation HR@10 of 0.4012, below the supplied 0.505 baseline by 0.1038. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.430, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.430, Electronics 0.275, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.470. Electronics was the weakest category. These results do not support this configuration of the attentive-history hypothesis. Limited order modeling, separate input/output embeddings, and the ranking objective are plausible contributors, but this trial cannot isolate their effects. Allocated GPU time was 202.43 seconds; epoch counts and convergence diagnostics were not supplied.
code_summary: Trains one independent HistoryModel per category with seed 42. Each network uses 128-dimensional input/output item embeddings, the latest item, mean history pooling, and two latest-item-conditioned attention pools with learned recency decay over up to 100 items. An MLP, residual mean connection, and LayerNorm produce a normalized context; normalized item scores include a jointly learned scale and item bias. Training samples history prefixes and uses 64 uniform negatives with equally mixed uniform and detached hard-negative weighting in a pairwise softplus loss, optimized by AdamW. Validation selects exactly one checkpoint per category. The generated predictor loads the matching architecture and checkpoint with all four dataset routes preserved; no ensemble or separately fitted scoring component is used.
